title: Fidelity & Cost Telemetry Advisor: Launch Brief and Playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:

This brief defines the product scope, acceptance criteria, launch steps, and go-to-market signals for the Fidelity & Cost Telemetry Advisor (FCTA) — a lightweight advisor service surfaced in Console and via API that recommends fidelity (model variant, quantization, batching) and pricing/packaging guidance based on live telemetry and customer goals. The target release is a controlled launch to pilot customers with a wider availability in Q3 2026.

Background and problem statement:
- Customers struggle to tune fidelity vs. cost tradeoffs for production inference. Current approaches are manual (trial-and-error) or require deep engineering investment.
- Platform telemetry contains rich signals (latency distributions, token-per-request distributions, KV cache hit rates, warm-start ratios, error rates) that can be turned into actionable fidelity recommendations.

Goals and non-goals:
1. Goals:
   - Surface per-route fidelity recommendations that reduce per-token cost by 10–30% while keeping customer-defined quality constraints (BLEU/ROUGE/QA delta) within tolerance.
   - Provide clear, actionable rollout steps (canary traffic split, metric watchers, rollback triggers).
   - Integrate with pricing engine to estimate monthly $ savings and recommended packaging options (microbundle, warm-capacity suggestion).
2. Non-goals:
   - This release will not provide automated model-level retraining nor automated quantization of customer models.
   - The advisor will not automatically change production traffic (manual approval required).

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Pilot adoption: 6 pilot customers onboarded within 8 weeks.
- Cost impact: mean recommended cost delta of -18% (median).
- Safety: <2% of recommendations that trigger a critical quality regression in monitored prompt sets during pilot.
- UX: >70% of pilot users follow the advisor rollout playbook for at least one route.

High-level user experience:
- Console: Route details -> "Fidelity Advisor" tab shows current telemetry snapshot, recommendation card with expected cost delta, quality risk score, and one-click exportable rollout checklist.
- API: POST /v1/advisor/evaluate with route_id and target_goal -> returns a list of discrete recommendation objects (variant, quant profile, batch_size, cache_policy) plus estimated monthly delta.

Functional requirements (priority ordered):
1) Telemetry ingestion and enrichment (MUST)
   - Ingest the following signals at 1m granularity: p50/p95 latency, tokens/request histogram, kv-cache-hit-rate, warm-start-rate, concurrency, error-rate by status code.
   - Augment with model profile: architecture family, seq-length-distribution, quantization-capable-flag.
2) Recommendation engine (MUST)
   - Rule-based baseline engine that encodes guardrails (latency SLO, quality shield thresholds).
   - Scoring model component (LOWER PRIORITY) that ranks options by cost/quality pareto front.
3) Console surface (MUST)
   - Recommendation card, confidence band, expected cost delta, manual rollout checklist export (markdown/JSON).
4) Pricing integration (MUST)
   - Call pricing service to simulate monthly billing under recommended config and present delta and suggested packaging options.
5) Rollout playbook (MUST)
   - Provide numbered rollout steps with explicit SLO checks and rollback criteria.
6) Audit & approval (MUST)
   - Store recommendations and owner approvals in the audit log (immutable for 90 days).
7) Safety testing harness (SHOULD)
   - Run recommended config against a sampled prompt set (tenant-mapped) in a sandbox and compute quality deltas before approval.
8) Multi-tenant isolation (MUST)
   - Ensure no cross-tenant telemetry mixing; customer data stays scoped to tenant.

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency of generating a recommendation: < 2s for common routes, < 10s for heavy analytic routes.
- Storage: telemetry retention 90 days in hot store, 13 months in cold store.
- Availability: 99.9% for advisor API during business hours, 99.5% globally.
- Security/compliance: support KMS-encrypted tenant ids and RBAC for action approvals.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Start with deterministic rules (quantize when token-lengths < 1024 and latency headroom > 20ms) to reduce initial ML model complexity and increase explainability.
- Use conservative default confidence bands: only recommend aggressive quant or variant demotion when sandbox pass-rate > 95%.
- Cost simulations will be approximate at launch (rounded to the nearest dollar for the customer view) and will include a margin of safety (+5%) in the presented savings.

Example recommendation (JSON snippet):
```
POST /v1/advisor/evaluate
{
  "route_id": "tenant-1234/route-payments",
  "target_goal": "cost-minimize",
  "constraints": { "max_quality_delta": 0.02, "latency_p95_target_ms": 250 }
}

RESPONSE 200
[
  {
    "recommendation_id": "rec-20260530-01",
    "variant": "redwood-compat-7b-quant8",
    "batch_size": 8,
    "kv_cache_policy": "prefix-cache:enabled",
    "expected_monthly_delta_usd": "-1200",
    "confidence": "high",
    "sandbox_pass_rate": "98%"
  }
]
```

Rollout checklist (exportable):
1. Create canary route with 5% traffic -> owner: eng-platform oncall
2. Monitor p50/p95 latency and quality monitors for 48 hours (triggers: latency_p95 > baseline + 20%, quality_regression > 1%) -> owner: route-owners
3. If safe, increase to 25% for 24 hours, then 100% if no triggers.
4. Post-rollout: schedule 7-day cost and quality review and update alert thresholds.

Packaging & pricing guidance (customer-facing options):
- Microbundle suggestion: If expected monthly savings > $1000, recommend microbundle upgrade for reduced per-token price.
- Warm capacity suggestion: If recommendations increase peak concurrency stability and customer has frequent traffic spikes, recommend a warm-capacity subscription estimate with monthly delta.

Pricing estimator table (display formatting shown as plain text):
| Scenario | Current monthly $ | Recommended monthly $ | Estimated savings | Suggested package |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Low-volume sandbox | 1,200 | 950 | 250 | none |
| Mid SaaS app | 6,400 | 5,120 | 1,280 | microbundle-standard |
| High-throughput | 35,000 | 28,000 | 7,000 | warm-capacity-committed |

Release plan and timeline (high level):
- Week 0–4: Build telemetry adapters, rule engine prototype, console UX mockups. Owned by: eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform, product UX.
- Week 5–8: Integrate pricing simulator, audit logging, and sandbox harness. Security review and RBAC scoping.
- Week 9: Onboard 3 internal beta tenants.
- Week 10–14: Pilot with 6 external customers. Collect feedback, measure KPIs.
- Week 15: Wider availability gating decision. Launch comms and pricing page updates.

Owner & runbook responsibilities:
- Product (Maya Patel) — overall program owner and PM for pilot coordination.
- Eng-serving-runtime — telemetry adapter and low-latency recommendation endpoint.
- Eng-platform — Console tab and rollout automation hooks.
- Eng-infra/security — KMS, RBAC, audit-log storage.
- Customer Success — pilot recruiting and onboarding playbook.

Operational runbook (short):
1. If advisor API error-rate > 2% for 10m, escalate to eng-serving-runtime oncall and switch advisor UI to "temporarily unavailable" mode.
2. If cost estimator deviates from billing by >10% for 3 customers, open an incident and pause billing-linked recommendations until corrected.
3. For quality regression incidents traced to advisor recommendations, roll back route configuration and flag the recommendation as failed. Notify product and research.

Dependencies and open questions:
- Pricing service endpoints and SLA for simulation calls (work with finance).
- Tenant-specific prompt sets for sandbox safety tests (agreement from customers required).
- Definitive success thresholds for quality metrics across verticals (PLG SaaS vs. regulated enterprise).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-aggressive recommendations causing quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative confidence bands, mandatory sandbox pass and manual approval.
- Risk: Billing mismatch leading to customer distrust. Mitigation: use conservative rounding and a disclaimer; prioritize reconciliations and telemetry alignment.

Appendix — Minimal acceptance checklist (for launch):
- Telemetry signals available for pilot tenants (yes/no)
- Pricing simulator integrated and vetted by finance (yes/no)
- Console UX validated in user tests (3 participants) (yes/no)
- Audit log writes verified for 90-day retention (yes/no)
- RBAC and approval flow reviewed by security (yes/no)
